title: Incident escalation cards and postmortem quick-links – Console prototype & review
creator: Arianna Cole
description:
Summary:
This ticket contains design work and prototypes for two related Console flows: (1) an Escalation Card component surfaced in alert rules and live incident panels to make on-call handoffs and escalation paths visible and actionable; and (2) Postmortem Quick-Links surfaced on incident pages and alert summaries so engineers and PMs can create, link, or jump to retrospective artifacts (Confluence, Drive, GitHub issues) with one click. The work aims to reduce cognitive load during incidents, shorten mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), and make post-incident follow-up consistent across teams.

Scope and goals:
- Design a compact Escalation Card that shows primary on-call, next escalations, contact method (Slack, PagerDuty, email), and an action menu (handoff, add note, escalate).
- Surface a cost-impact badge and SLO health snippet within the card to help triage severity vs business impact.
- Provide a Postmortem Quick-Links area: Create PM template, Link existing postmortem, Add internal notes, and Attach GitHub PR or incident runbook.
- Ensure these components work in 3 console contexts: Alerts list, Active Incident page, Historical Incident detail.
- Meet accessibility requirements (WCAG AA) for contrast and keyboard navigation.

Key design decisions and trade-offs:
- Progressive disclosure: keep Escalation Card compact by default; expand to full detail on click to avoid overwhelming dashboards. Trade-off: extra click for deep info vs. cleaner UI in high-density views.
- Read-only vs editable escalation policies: the first iteration is read-only with an explicit "Request change" flow that opens Dedicated policy editor (engineering dependency). Rationale: avoid coupling UX to backend policy edit API in this sprint.
- Cost impact shown as a normalized 0–100 indicator + currency delta; rationale is quick prioritization. Trade-off with data freshness — cost numbers are pulled from analytics with a 5-minute lag.
- Postmortem quick-links include a lightweight "Create draft" flow that opens a modal prefilled with incident metadata; full authoring handled in external doc (Confluence/Drive) to avoid building rich text surfaces in Console at this time.

Component breakdown and specs (for dev handoff):
- Escalation Card (compact): avatar(s), primary on-call name, method icons (Slack/PD/email), short SLO chip (green/yellow/red), cost-impact micrograph, overflow menu (3 actions).
- Escalation Card (expanded): timeline of escalation steps, timestamps, last-handoff note, button: "Initiate handoff" (opens ephemeral modal), link: "Open escalation policy" (requires permission).
- Postmortem Quick-Links: status chip (none/linked/draft), primary action button (Create Link / Open / Create Draft), secondary menu with Add PR, Attach Runbook, Add Postmortem Owner.
- Incident header changes: small affordance to surface both components without increasing header height (use stacked microselections).

Interaction and microcopy samples:
- Handoff confirmation: "Transfer primary on-call to @name? A notification will be sent to Slack and PagerDuty."
- Create draft CTA: "Create Postmortem draft with incident summary and timeline — editable after creation."
- Escalate CTA: "Escalate to next policy step and notify on-call team."

Accessibility notes:
- All action buttons keyboard-focusable; Escalation Card expandable region uses aria-expanded and role="region" with label.
- Color-only SLO indicators have redundant labels and icons.
- Avatar elements include aria-label with full person name and contact method.

Telemetry and analytics (events for Eng):
- escalation.card.viewed, escalation.card.expanded, escalation.handoff.initiated, postmortem.link.created, postmortem.draft.created, postmortem.link.opened. Each event should include incident_id, alert_rule_id, user_id, and environment (hosted|dedicated|private).

Acceptance criteria (design):
- Figma prototypes for Alerts list, Active Incident, and Historical Incident are linked and clickable.
- Microcopy reviewed and approved by PM.
- Accessibility checklist passed in internal QA with contrast and keyboard flow validated.
- Engineering tasks created for implementation with clear props/interface for components and telemetry.

Handoff notes for engineering:
- This version is presentational; escalation policy edits are out-of-scope but must include a CTA that opens policy editor route: /console/policies/:id.
- Cost impact data contract: {"incident_cost_estimate_usd": number, "window_minutes": number} — engineering please confirm field names.
- Suggested feature flags: feature:incident_escalation_v1, feature:postmortem_quicklinks_v1.

Next steps and rollout plan:
- Incorporate design feedback from PM (complete) and Eng (in-progress).
- Finalize Figma prototypes and upload component tokens to the design system.
- Create engineering stories: ENG-2431 (Escalation Card component), ENG-2432 (Postmortem Quick-Links backend hooks), ENG-2433 (Telemetry).
- Ship behind feature flag and run canary for 10% of traffic, monitor MTTA and manual handoffs for two weeks, then ramp.

Notes on uniqueness for future reference:
- This work is intentionally lightweight on editing and heavy on surfacing actionable links to reduce incident cognitive overhead. We avoid building a full editor in Console in this iteration.
